Reading the files I need to touch first. Now read DealList and ProofPage for the unlisted-token fallback work: Good — I have everything. Now also check the hooks file for `useGoodsTokenMeta` which I'll need for DealList unlisted-token fallback: Good. Now I have a complete picture. Setting up todos: **Item 1 — Homepage copy sweep:** Also update the `index.html` meta description if it exists: Good, no stablecoin wording in index.html. Now also update the `STEPS` array step 3 copy which says "Collect your tokens" — that's fine. And the seller FAQ entry says "choose the token you are offering" — that's already generic. Done with item 1.

**Item 2 — Stats band: full-width row under hero, large numbers:** Reorder STATS to the specified order (Volume, Units sold, Buyers, Deals, Saved by buyers), then replace the hero section with one-column headline + full-width stats band underneath: Now replace the entire hero section (the `<section>` with hero + old stats sidebar) with a one-column hero followed by a full-width stats band: Good. The `divide-x divide-y` Tailwind classes need the border color — Tailwind's divide utilities use `currentColor` by default, so I need to make sure the theme variable works. I'll add explicit `[--tw-divide-color:var(--border)]` or use the `style` prop approach. Actually Tailwind v3 `divide-y` just adds border-top to children — I'll override with a CSS custom prop or just remove the Tailwind dividers and use `border-r`/`border-b` inline via style. Simplest: use a wrapper style and explicit border rendering per cell via `border-r last:border-r-0`: Actually the border logic is complex to reason about correctly at all breakpoints. Let me simplify: remove inline borders and just use a single background-image approach, or better — use `after:` rings inside the grid. Simplest and most correct: just use `gap-px` on the grid with a background on the wrapper to act as dividers: That's the cleanest approach. The `overflow-hidden` on the outer card clips the gap-px edges so there are no stray border lines outside.

**Item 3 — Custom token address input:** The custom token work is self-contained in `SupplierView.tsx`. I'll:

1. Add a `CustomToken` type that extends `GoodsToken` with an `unverified` flag
2. Change `selectedToken` state type to `GoodsToken | CustomToken`
3. Add address input state to the dropdown component (passed in via props)
4. Add a `useReadContracts` call that reads `symbol`, `name`, `decimals`, `balanceOf` for the entered address
5. Propagate validation state (loading / error / resolved) up via a callback
6. When resolved and address matches a `GOODS_TOKENS` entry, select that entry instead
7. Show unverified amber notice in the main form when `selectedToken.unverified` is set
8. Gate market buttons on `!selectedToken.unverified`

First, update the types and the `TokenPickerDropdown` component: Now add the `CustomToken` type and update the picker interface: Now replace the `TokenPickerDropdown` component with one that includes the "Other token…" option and the address input: Now update the main component: change `selectedToken` type to `AnyToken`, update the picker call site with `walletAddr`, add the unverified badge, and gate market buttons: Now update the picker call site to pass `walletAddr` and use stable `onSelect` callback: Now add the unverified amber notice directly after the picker and gate the market-price buttons. Add after the zero-balance notice: Now gate `mUsdPerToken` and the market buttons on `!isCustomToken(selectedToken)`. The `mSym` is derived from `selectedToken.marketSymbol` — custom tokens don't have `marketSymbol` so `mUsdPerToken` will naturally be `undefined`. That's already correct since `GoodsToken.marketSymbol` is optional. But `isCustomToken` check is cleanest. The `marketPricePerUnit` will be null if `mUsdPerToken` is undefined, so the "Use market price" button and "Set to market" buttons are already hidden. The rate label check `mUsdPerToken !== undefined && ratesAgeLabel` also hides naturally. So no additional gating is needed — the `marketSymbol?: string` being absent on custom tokens handles it all.

However the `mSym` derivation accesses `selectedToken.marketSymbol` — `GoodsToken` already has `marketSymbol?: string` so custom tokens (which extend `GoodsToken`) inherit that optional field; it will just be `undefined`. Good.

Now also update the balance batch calls — the custom token needs to be excluded from the GOODS_TOKENS batch (since we handle its balance separately in the picker). The current `balanceCalls` only iterates `GOODS_TOKENS` which is fine. The custom token's balance is injected directly into `allBalances` via `balances.set()` inside `resolvedCustom` memo in the picker — but that mutates the `Map` that was passed in, which is derived from `allBalancesRaw` each render, so the mutation is lost next render. I need a different approach: hold custom token balance in a separate ref/state accessible to the main component.

The cleanest fix: instead of mutating `balances` inside the picker, expose a `customBalance` state from the picker up to the parent, or simply read the custom token balance separately in the main component when `selectedToken` is custom.

Let me add a `useReadContracts` call in the main component for the custom token's balance when it's selected: Now update the picker call site to use `allBalancesWithCustom`: Now remove the stale mutation of `balances` in the picker's `resolvedCustom` memo (that was the old approach — now balance comes from the main component's separate read): Remove unused `balances` from `resolvedCustom` deps since we no longer use it there: The picker still uses `balances` in the render for display (showing balances per row in the dropdown list) — that's fine, it's the `allBalancesWithCustom` map passed from the parent which includes the custom balance. The `balances` parameter in the picker is now read-only display. Good.

**Item 4 — DealList and ProofPage: on-chain fallback for unlisted tokens:**

For `DealList`, I need `tokenSymbol` and `tokenDecimals` for unlisted tokens. The current code does `tokenConfig?.decimals` which returns `undefined` for unknown tokens — `PricePerToken` already handles `tokenDecimals === undefined` gracefully. The main issue is `tokenSymbol` shows `'?'` for unknown tokens. I'll use `useGoodsTokenMeta` but it's a hook that can't be called inside a map. The right approach: extract `DealCard` already calls hooks (it's its own component) — so I can call `useGoodsTokenMeta` inside `DealCard` when `tokenConfig` is undefined. Now update `DealCard` to call `useGoodsTokenMeta` for unlisted tokens: Now update `ProofPage` — the `GoodsClaimed` event summary uses `tok.decimals` and shows `String(a.amount) tokens` for unlisted tokens. I can't call a hook inside the `switch` in `EventSummary`, so I'll create a small `GoodsClaimedSummary` sub-component that calls `useGoodsTokenMeta`: Now replace the `GoodsClaimed` case in `EventSummary` with a call to a new sub-component: Now add the `GoodsClaimedSummary` component at the bottom of ProofPage.tsx: Now run the check: One warning: `balR` is declared but unused (we removed the balance mutation). Prefix it with `_`: Zero warnings, zero errors. Here is what changed:

**Homepage (items 1 + 2):**
- Hero subtitle and FAQ "What can I buy?" entry now say "assets on Arc" instead of "stablecoins and tokens".
- Stats moved out of the sidebar entirely. The hero is now a single full-width column (headline, subtitle, two CTAs). Directly underneath is a full-width stats band: one shared card with a `gap-px` grid (5 equal columns on desktop, 2+1 on phone) — the `gap-px` + border-colour background trick produces clean 1px dividers at every breakpoint with no per-cell border logic. Numbers are `text-4xl font-bold tabular-nums`, label underneath in muted text. Skeleton placeholders match the number size so there is no layout shift while loading. Order: Volume, Units sold, Buyers, Deals, Saved by buyers.

**Sell page — custom token (item 3):**
- Token dropdown now has an "Other token…" entry at the bottom of the list.
- Choosing it reveals an address input. On a valid `0x` address, one `useReadContracts` multicall reads `symbol`, `name`, `decimals`, and a sanity check; if any call fails or `decimals > 36` the error message "This address isn't a standard token on Arc." is shown and Post stays disabled.
- If the address matches a `GOODS_TOKENS` entry the picker silently switches to that listed token (no unverified badge).
- For a genuinely new token, an amber notice is shown: "Unverified token. Check the address is the one you mean. Tokens that take a fee on transfer or change balances on their own will not work with Swarm."
- The custom token's balance is read separately in the main component (not hacked into the `allBalances` map) and merged cleanly.
- Market-price buttons (`mSym` / `mUsdPerToken`) are absent for custom tokens because `marketSymbol` is undefined — they hide automatically without extra gating.

**DealList + ProofPage — unlisted token fallback (item 3 tail):**
- `DealCard` now calls `useGoodsTokenMeta` when the deal's `goodsToken` address is not in `GOODS_TOKENS`, so the card shows the real symbol and uses the real decimal count for `PricePerToken`.
- `ProofPage` `GoodsClaimed` event rows are rendered by a new `GoodsClaimedSummary` component that similarly calls `useGoodsTokenMeta` for unlisted tokens, formatting the amount with the correct decimals instead of showing a raw bigint.
